# Greek letters {#sec-greek}

::: {style="margin-top: 1em; font-size: 125%; font-weight: 1000; text-align: center;"}
The one like the fish.
:::

Once, a colleague gave a lecture on Lotka-Volterra equation to undergraduate students in the biology department. When a student asked: "what is alpha?", she spent a few minutes explaining what alpha represented until another student interjected and said: "it is the one like the fish". It was a wake up call that understanding greek letter is a problem. And to the majority it is the case, so let's clear that out.

This is unfamiliar $(\zeta  + \xi)^2 = \zeta^2 + \xi^2 + 2\zeta\xi$, yet the *identité remarquable* $(a + b) ^ 2 = a^2 + b^2 + 2ab$

Roman notation is also impossible to do $XIII + IX = XXII$, while this $13 + 9 = 22$ is trivial

A major barrier to is inability to go past beyond notation. While in the right context, using roman number feels normal when siting section in the bible. First because we are used to it, but second because we understand the specific choice (separete section and verse).

So as every notation: greek letter are used with convience (not a necessity), and as with roman numbers, habits, basic comprehension are elements to be comfortable with them

## Formal {.unnumbered}

Here is dictionary of the greek alphabet in upper and lower case, the latin equivalent, and how to call them

| Lower Case | Upper Case | Latin Equivalent | Name    |
|:-----------|:-----------|:-----------------|:--------|
| $\alpha$   | $A$        | a                | Alpha   |
| $\beta$    | $B$        | b                | Beta    |
| $\gamma$   | $\Gamma$   | g                | Gamma   |
| $\delta$   | $\Delta$   | d                | Delta   |
| $\epsilon$ | $E$        | e                | Epsilon |
| $\zeta$    | $Z$        | z                | Zeta    |
| $\eta$     | $H$        | e                | Eta     |
| $\theta$   | $\Theta$   | th               | Theta   |
| $\iota$    | $I$        | i                | Iota    |
| $\kappa$   | $K$        | k                | Kappa   |
| $\lambda$  | $\Lambda$  | l                | Lambda  |
| $\mu$      | $M$        | m                | Mu      |
| $\nu$      | $N$        | n                | Nu      |
| $\xi$      | $\Xi$      | x                | Xi      |
| $\omicron$ | $O$        | o                | Omicron |
| $\pi$      | $\Pi$      | p                | Pi      |
| $\rho$     | $R$        | r                | Rho     |
| $\sigma$   | $\Sigma$   | s                | Sigma   |
| $\tau$     | $T$        | t                | Tau     |
| $\upsilon$ | $\Upsilon$ | y                | Upsilon |
| $\phi$     | $\Phi$     | ph               | Phi     |
| $\chi$     | $X$        | ch               | Chi     |
| $\psi$     | $\Psi$     | ps               | Psi     |
| $\omega$   | $\Omega$   | o                | Omega   |


## Examples {.unnumbered}
- "I am $\alpha$ and $\Omega$", probably the most famous use of greek letters to mean beginning and the end.
- $\pi$ represents the number 3.14 etc We could also think that $\pi$ is the ratio between the circumference and diameter. So it represents a constant
- $\sigma$ is used as the parameter for standard deviation for a normal distribution. The variance is $\sigma^2$.
- $\Sigma$ and $\Pi$ are used for shortcut summation and product see @sec-sum.
- $\Omega$ is usually used to represent a set, but can mean something else in physics.
- $\zeta$ is one of famous equation that mathematicians are hoping to solove
- $\epsilon$ and $\omicron$ $\iota$ etc are something small

## Tips and warning {.unnumbered}
- Greek letters are used to show difference.
  - In statistics, difference between true value ($\sigma$) for standard deviation of the [population](@sec-population) vs. $s$ for estimated value from the sample.
  - In mathematics: greek could represend parameter while represent variable $\mu$ is for mortallity instead x, y, for variable and t for time.
- Use of greek letter for paremeters in probability: $N(\mu, \sigma)$ or Poisson($\lambda$)
- Use of greek letters for covid variants.
- Latin browed letters from Greek. When the romans picked the letter, some of them were dropped because romans did not need them (like phi) or modified them, Delta, Lambda and sigma. while some kept the same.
